subject.title: feat(webui): reintroduce opt-in AI purpose titles for tool calls

question: Should OpenClaw accept an opt-in core Control UI feature that sends redacted tool-call content to a utility model and adds configuration, protocol, token-spend, and cache surface for decorative titles?
rationale: The implementation defects have concrete fixes, but only maintainers can decide whether this optional readability benefit justifies the permanent core privacy, compatibility, and support footprint.

options.title: Accept after fixes and proof
options.body: Keep the default off, repair context and auth ownership, resolve conflicts, and require exact-head live evidence before merge.

options.title: Keep deterministic rendering only
options.body: Close the proposal and retain current main’s model-free tool activity UI.

options.title: Redesign a narrower mechanism
options.body: Pause and pursue deterministic or client-local summaries without provider calls and a new gateway RPC.

recommendation.title: Accept after fixes and proof
recommendation.body: Keep the default off, repair context and auth ownership, resolve conflicts, and require exact-head live evidence before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the complete feature history and are best positioned to decide whether the core surface is worth accepting.
